children: Microsoft is having a bad few days, not quite Nvidia levels of bad but far from ideal.

A global outage has hit the company's Outlook, Teams, and Copilot AI assistant, impacting users across more than 70 countries, according to outage tracker Downdetector. More than 430 million people use Microsoft 365 services, as well as governments and organizations around the world.
The stock was down 0.6% in early trading Friday, recovering from a drop of more than 2% in premarket trading.
The timing of the outage is particularly inconvenient for Microsoft. Anthropic launched a new suite of office tools on Tuesday and the market saw it as a direct challenge to the tech giant.

Engineers have been working to fix the problem for more than 20 hours, but regular updates show it's been a struggle.  "We've monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected," the company said in a status update shortly after 10 p.m. Eastern time Thursday, more than nine hours after first confirming it was investigating the issue.

Microsoft reported improvements in service availability and email queues significantly reducing toward normal levels, in its most recent update at around 9 a.m. Eastern time. However, it said some users may still experience intermittent access or delayed email delivery.
The company added that it had "no evidence of malicious activity associated with this incident," at this time.
It's been a tough week for the tech giant. Reports of OpenAI's latest figures suggested that it's some way behind Anthropic in the AI race.
That's bad news for Microsoft, which has a 24% stake in the OpenAI and a much smaller investment in Anthropic.
